observed_title: Hacking Jenkins Part 2 - Abusing Meta Programming for Unauthenticated RCE!

retrieval.quote_verification: Exact, unnormalized document.body.textContent inclusion and matching paragraph.textContent checks in the original article DOM using agent_browser --session orange-O021 eval. All four quotes matched; the figure immediately following E2 was also checked for the explicitly shown objdump disassembly. Title and section headings were checked in the DOM.

reason: The article supplies distinct reusable method evidence beyond its omitted exploit: questioning parse-only safety through phase-specific side effects, using generated instructions to attribute computation to a phase, diagnosing an integrated-environment dependency failure, and distinguishing compile-time behavior from runtime sandbox coverage.

evidence.locator: How to Exploit? (How-to-Exploit), opening paragraph asking about compilation/parsing side effects
evidence.quote: Compiling(or parsing) is a hard work with lots of tough things and hidden features. So, the idea is, is there any side effect we can leverage?

evidence.locator: How to Exploit? (How-to-Exploit), paragraph after the compile-time calculation illustration and immediately before the objdump disassembly listing
evidence.quote: From the assembly language of compiled binary, we can make sure the result is calculated at compile-time, not run-time!

evidence.locator: First Attempt (First-Attempt), root-cause paragraph beginning 'With a little bit digging, we found the root cause.'
evidence.quote: As a result, the problem become lack of corresponding library in classPath during compile-time.

evidence.locator: Epilogue (Epilogue), opening paragraph contrasting the sandbox's runtime coverage with compile-time behavior
evidence.quote: Although there is a built-in Groovy Sandbox(Script Security Plugin) on Jenkins to protect the Pipeline, it’s useless because the vulnerability is in compile-time, not in run-time!

workflow.decision: When an operation is described as parse-only, ask which preparation phases can have side effects instead of equating absence of ordinary execution with inert processing. Use phase documentation and a narrow implementation slice to formulate a phase-specific hypothesis.

To distinguish compilation-time computation from runtime computation, inspect the generated instructions for a benign example and compare them with the expected precomputed result. Establish the phase before attributing capabilities to it.

If a standalone observation fails in an integrated environment, explain the first phase-specific dependency or class-loading failure. Preserve that environment difference as a prerequisite rather than treating the failure as general safety or the local success as portable proof.

For a claimed sandbox, map each guard to the phase it actually covers. Behavior in an earlier phase is a separate boundary question; preserve independent reachability and confinement gates instead of declaring all isolation ineffective.

tools.purpose: Inspect generated instructions to distinguish a compilation-time computed value from runtime computation.
tools.when: A benign compilation illustration needs phase attribution; its disassembly does not establish service reachability or security-policy coverage.

handoffs.when: An allegedly inert validation path has an unresolved preparation-phase effect or a standalone/integrated behavior mismatch.

handoffs.acceptance_gate: The benign observation must distinguish the predicted phases under a documented baseline; a configuration change cannot silently substitute for the original environment. Reject a packet that contains only an alarming API name or an unexplained dependency error.

handoffs.acceptance_gate: Identify the exact phase and enforcement location before assessing coverage. The consumer may analyze a source-only hypothesis but must not promote it to a demonstrated sandbox escape or unauthenticated impact.

limitations: This is a historical 2019 Jenkins/Groovy account. Vulnerability and impact statements remain author reports; no code execution, target interaction, present-release check or shipped-fix verification was performed.

The first standalone result failed in the integrated service because a compile-time library dependency was unavailable. An administrator-controlled configuration change would alter the evaluated claim and cannot establish default-environment portability.
The explicit objdump usage belongs to a C++ compile-time calculation illustration, not a verification of the service's behavioral reachability.

Compile-time versus runtime coverage does not by itself establish unauthenticated reachability. Permission requirements and the separately linked routing issue remain distinct, unverified prerequisites; this packet retains no chain to overcome them.

candidate_additions.guidance: Do not classify validation, parsing or compilation as inert merely because ordinary program execution is absent. Enumerate the processing phases and user-influenced preparation hooks, then state a falsifiable side-effect invariant.

For standalone versus integrated discrepancies, locate the first phase-specific dependency failure and compare module availability and class-loading context. Record configuration changes separately; neither an unexplained failure nor a modified-environment success resolves original-environment feasibility.

Make the policy-layer table phase-aware: an execution-time guard is not evidence that preparation-time behavior is constrained. Require phase-specific enforcement evidence and preserve all remaining authorization and isolation restrictions.
